threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and initial task ownership for the playbook project.

messages.text: Kicking off the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout project_title. Goal is to have a unified playbook, scripts, and training ready for a one-month pilot, using existing CRM only. For scope: T1 and T3 on the contact centre side, T2 and T4 on the sales side. For KPIs, my first pass for the pilot, to be tracked in A4, is: 1) conversion rate from qualified lead to sale, 2) first contact resolution for top 5 reasons, 3) average handle time with a guardrail so we do not rush calls, 4) contact quality score from monitoring, 5) data completeness in CRM mandatory fields. Can you react in this thread with any must-have KPIs I missed and confirm you are ok owning your tasks T1–T4 so we can lock D1 and D2 later today

Thanks for framing this. From the sales side I am comfortable owning T2 and T4. For KPIs, I would add: 6) opportunity qualification rate, based on how often A2 is fully completed, and 7) follow-up SLA adherence for email and chat templates from T4. These can also live in A4 so we have a single view. On scope, just confirming we are not touching CRM configuration, only usage guidelines and scripts, correct

Correct, no CRM config changes in this phase, only guidance and playbook content. Good call on qualification rate and follow-up SLA. That gives us a more complete view of the funnel. For T1 and T3, I can take primary ownership but will need input from both of you on sales handovers and compliance wording. I will draft a simple RACI after we confirm owners in D2.

I can support on T1 and T3 with mapping the current inbound and outbound flows and pulling a first list of top 5 contact reasons from our reports. I will need a bit of help validating the pain points and making sure they line up with the sales stages. For KPIs, should we also track transfer rate between contact centre and sales so we see if the new playbook reduces unnecessary transfers

On T4, I am happy to help draft some of the email and chat templates, especially for follow-up and escalation. I will probably need guidance on the exact wording for compliance-sensitive parts. For KPIs, I like the idea of tracking follow-up SLA. Maybe we can also look at reply rate on follow-up emails, if that is easy to pull from the current CRM setup

I can support on T2 by sharing some of the questions I usually ask on calls and in meetings. I am not fully sure how to turn that into a formal checklist though, so I might need someone to structure it into A2. On KPIs, I do not have anything to add beyond what you all listed.

Transfer rate is a good one. We can track: 8) percentage of contacts transferred from contact centre to sales, and 9) conversion rate on those transferred contacts. That will show if the new escalation rules are working. I will check with our CRM admin that these can be pulled easily into A4 without new fields.

Reply rate on follow-up emails is useful, as long as we can get it from existing reports. Let us tentatively include it and confirm feasibility when we define T6 later. For now, for D1, the candidate KPI list for the pilot is: 1) conversion rate from qualified lead to sale, 2) first contact resolution for top 5 reasons, 3) average handle time, 4) contact quality score, 5) CRM data completeness, 6) opportunity qualification rate, 7) follow-up SLA adherence, 8) transfer rate from contact centre to sales, 9) conversion on transferred contacts, 10) reply rate on follow-up emails. Please react with thumbs up if you are ok with this list, or comment if anything is missing or not realistic.

This list looks solid to me. From a sales perspective, it covers both volume and quality. Only question is whether we want to split conversion rate by channel, but that might be overkill for the first pilot.

I am ok with the KPI list as is. Splitting by channel would be nice to have, but I agree we can start simple and add that later if reporting allows. From the contact centre side, these are all measurable with what we have today.
No objections from me. It will be helpful if we get a simple view of these KPIs in A4 so we can see progress week by week during the pilot.
I am aligned with the KPI list. I will take the action to translate these into a tab structure in A4 and confirm with CRM admin that all data points are available without new fields.

Great, then for D1 we are confirming the KPI list you summarised, to be tracked in A4 for the pilot. On D2, let us confirm task ownership and initial target dates: T1 and T3 primary owner me, with support from 269042; T2 primary owner 29962 with input from 356759; T4 primary owner 379361 with support from 29962. Proposal on timing: T1 and T2 by end of this week, T3 and T4 by mid next week so we have time for review. Please confirm or suggest adjustments.
I am ok supporting you on T1 and T3 with that timing. I can start mapping the current journeys tomorrow and share a draft for you to refine before we validate with sales.

I can send my list of qualification questions for T2 by tomorrow, so 29962 can structure them into the checklist. I might need a bit more time if we expect me to draft full wording, so I prefer to focus on content input.

I am good to own T4 with support from 29962. Mid next week works for me. I will start with introduction and follow-up templates, then we can iterate on closing and escalation once T2 and T3 are more defined.

Confirmed on my side: I will own T2 and support T4. End of this week for a first draft of A2 is realistic. I will also start sketching the structure for T4 templates so we keep tone and stages consistent.

Thanks all. For D2, we are confirming: T1 and T3 owned by me with support from 269042, T2 owned by 29962 with input from 356759, and T4 owned by 379361 with support from 29962, with the target dates we discussed. I will summarise these in our project tracker and link back to this thread.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise scripts, qualification checklist, and CRM guidelines.

messages.text: Sharing draft materials for review so we can move toward sign-off: 1) A2 draft for T2, 2) first version of call scripts for top 5 reasons from T3, to be added into A5, and 3) CRM usage and mandatory fields guide for T5, to become A3. These will all roll into A1. Please use this thread to comment on clarity, practicality, and any compliance concerns. Once we address feedback, we will aim to close D3 for the checklist and D4 for the scripts.

I went through the drafts. On A2, the structure looks good, but I suggest we explicitly flag which questions are mandatory for compliance versus recommended for deeper discovery. That will help agents prioritise under time pressure. On the T3 scripts, we need to double-check a couple of phrases against consumer protection wording; I will run those by our compliance officer before we call them final. For A3, the mandatory fields per interaction type align with current CRM config, which is key for our constraint.

From the contact centre side, A2 feels a bit long for shorter inbound calls. Maybe we can have a condensed version for quick enquiries and the full version for sales opportunities. For the T3 scripts, I like the flow, but I would add a short recap step before closing the call to confirm next actions. On A3, could we add a simple example for each interaction type so agents see what good data entry looks like

On the scripts that will go into A5, I noticed the tone is slightly different between sales-led and service-led scenarios. I can help harmonise the language so it feels like one voice across channels. For A2, I agree with having a core set of must-ask questions and then optional probes. That will also make it easier to align email and chat templates from T4.

I tried using the A2 draft on a couple of calls today. It helped structure the conversation, but I struggled to fit all questions in when the customer was in a hurry. Maybe we can mark a minimum set that must be covered on the first call and the rest can be completed in a follow-up. Also, I am not fully sure when to use each of the T3 scripts; a short decision tree in A1 would help.

Thanks for the detailed feedback. I will update A2 to clearly separate mandatory and optional questions and create a short version for quick inbound calls, as 269042 and 356759 suggested. For A3, I can add examples per interaction type. On scripts, I will work with 379361 to align tone and with 8337 to incorporate the recap step and route the sensitive phrases to the compliance officer.

I will take the action to send the updated T3 scripts to the compliance officer today and capture any required changes before we finalise A5. Once we have that feedback, we should be ready to sign off D4 for the initial script set for the pilot.
On A3, when you add examples, could you also highlight common mistakes we see today, like missing contact reason or vague notes. That will make the guidelines more concrete for agents.

I will start harmonising the language across the scripts and the email and chat templates from T4. Once we have the compliance feedback, I will do a final pass to ensure everything in A5 is consistent and easy to follow.

When you create the short version of A2, could you share a quick example of how to transition from the short to the full checklist in a follow-up call. I want to make sure I do not sound repetitive to the customer.
Good point. I will add a short script snippet into A2 and A5 for that transition, so it is clear how to pick up the remaining questions without frustrating the customer.

I have now incorporated all feedback into A2 and A3 and synced with 379361 on the script tone. 8337, once you confirm that the compliance officer is ok with the updated T3 scripts, I propose we formally approve A2 for the pilot so we can close D3.

Compliance review came back with minor wording tweaks, which I have already applied to the T3 scripts and reflected in A5. With that, I am comfortable saying the current A2 checklist is fit for purpose for the pilot, with clear mandatory and optional sections. For D3, I am approving A2 for use in the pilot, subject to further tweaks after we see real-world usage.
From the contact centre side, I am ok to start using the approved A2 in the pilot teams. The scripts in A5 also look ready to test, now that the recap step and compliance tweaks are in.

Agreed. The initial set of call, email, and chat scripts in A5 is coherent and covers the top 5 contact reasons plus the key sales stages. I suggest we treat them as version 1 for the pilot and capture feedback in our script review ritual.
Given the approvals and compliance sign-off, I propose we close D4 by confirming that the current A5 library is the initial script set for the pilot, to be refined after we collect data and feedback.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in training approach, schedule, and quality monitoring process.

messages.text: Sharing the draft training plan A7 for T7 and the quality monitoring checklist A6 for T11. The idea is to run short, focused sessions across shifts, with a mix of theory and call listening, and to use A6 as the standard for coaching on the new scripts in A5. In this thread, let us validate the schedule feasibility and the checklist content so we can close D5 on the training schedule and D6 on the quality checklist.

Looking at A7, the 90-minute sessions per group seem reasonable, but for the late shift we might need to split into two 45-minute blocks to avoid impacting service levels. For A6, I like that it maps directly to the new scripts, but I wonder if we should weight some items more heavily, like compliance statements and data capture, so they have more impact on the overall score.

From the sales side, A7 covers the right topics: using A2, applying A5 scripts, and updating A3 fields correctly. For account managers, we could probably do a single 2-hour deep dive instead of multiple shorter sessions, since we have more flexibility on scheduling. On A6, I would add one item on how well the agent sets up the handover to sales when criteria are met, since that is critical for our joint funnel.

I can help facilitate some of the training sessions, especially the parts on using A2 and the email and chat templates from A5. For A7, could we include a short practice block where agents draft a follow-up email or chat message based on a call scenario. That will make the content more concrete.

On the schedule in A7, I am a bit concerned about back-to-back sessions for some agents who already have coaching booked. Maybe we can publish the proposed slots early so supervisors can swap people around. For A6, I like the checklist, but I would appreciate a couple of example call evaluations so I know what a high score looks like.

Good points. I will adjust A7 so late shift sessions are split into two 45-minute blocks and add guidance for supervisors to avoid clashes with existing coaching. On A6, I can introduce weighting for critical items like compliance statements, mandatory disclosures, and CRM data completeness, and add a specific item for sales handover quality as 29962 suggested.

Splitting the late shift sessions will help a lot. For A6, once you add the weighting, could you also include a simple scoring example in A7 so supervisors know how to calculate and interpret the scores consistently.

On the training format, I am fine with the split sessions for agents and a single longer session for account managers. For D5, once you update A7 with these tweaks, I am comfortable locking the schedule so we can start inviting people.

I can draft a couple of example evaluations using A6, one strong call and one that needs improvement, and we can include them as annexes to A7. That should make it easier for supervisors and agents to understand expectations.
That would be very helpful, thanks. Seeing concrete examples will make it easier for me to adjust how I handle calls to match the new standards in A6.

I have now updated A7 with the split sessions for late shifts, the dedicated 2-hour block for account managers, and the practice exercises that 379361 suggested. I also added scoring examples for A6. Unless there are strong objections, I propose we confirm D5: this training schedule and format will be used for the pilot rollout.
I am aligned with the updated A7. The schedule works for our teams, and the content covers what agents need to start using A2, A3, and A5. No objections from my side to closing D5.
Confirmed from sales as well. The schedule in A7 is workable and aligns with our timelines for the pilot. Happy to treat D5 as closed.

On A6, I have now added weighting for critical behaviours, a specific item for sales handover quality, and clarified the review cadence: weekly for pilot teams, bi-weekly for others. I also aligned the checklist items with the latest A5 scripts. If there are no further comments, I suggest we approve A6 as the standard for the pilot and close D6.
The updated A6 looks good to me. The weighting and examples make it clear how to score calls, and the weekly cadence for pilot teams will give us enough data to adjust quickly.
Agreed. We can start using A6 with the pilot teams as soon as training is complete. No further changes needed from my side.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot rollout, including escalation paths and dashboards.

messages.text: Pilot update: we have identified one sales pod and one contact centre team to participate in the Unified Sales and Contact Centre Playbook Rollout project_title pilot. We now need to lock D7 on pilot scope and duration, and D8 on escalation criteria and SLAs for high-value leads. A4 is set up with the KPIs we agreed, and I have a draft for T6 metrics and T10 escalation paths. Please review the proposal below and comment in this thread.

For scope, I suggest we include all inbound and outbound calls for the selected contact centre team that fall into the top 5 contact reasons, plus all related email and chat interactions handled by the pilot sales pod. Duration-wise, a 4-week pilot should give us enough volume to see trends in A4. For T10, we need clear criteria for what counts as a high-value lead so agents are not guessing.

From the contact centre side, the proposed scope is manageable, as long as we keep the pilot to one team. For duration, 4 weeks works, but we should have a checkpoint after 2 weeks to see if any adjustments are needed. On escalation, I would like a simple rule of thumb in A1 so agents know when to escalate immediately versus schedule a follow-up.

On T6, I propose we track the KPIs we defined earlier in A4 with a weekly cadence, plus a simple qualitative feedback log from agents and account managers. For T10, my draft criteria for high-value leads are: deal size above a certain threshold, strategic accounts, and urgent time-bound opportunities. We can refine the thresholds with sales operations.

I am part of the pilot sales pod. For escalation SLAs, it would help to know exactly how fast we are expected to pick up high-value leads once they are passed from the contact centre. Also, will we get alerts from the CRM, or do we need to monitor a specific view manually

For SLAs, my proposal is: high-value leads should be contacted by the sales pod within 2 business hours during working time, and by 10am next business day if they come in after hours. We can use an existing CRM view filtered by the high-value flag and pilot team ownership, so no new configuration is needed. I will document this in T6 and T10.

The high-value criteria you listed make sense. We should also include cases where the customer explicitly asks to speak to sales about a purchase decision, even if the estimated deal size is not clear yet. I will make sure this is reflected in the scripts in A5 and in the escalation section of A1.

From the contact centre perspective, the 2-hour SLA is achievable as long as we have a clear process for flagging and assigning high-value leads in the CRM. We will need a short refresher for agents on how to do this during training.

I will update the escalation section in A1 and the relevant scripts in A5 to include that explicit customer request scenario. I will also add a short note in the email and chat templates so the handover is clear for the sales pod.

On T6, I have configured A4 to show weekly trends for all agreed KPIs, with separate tabs for contact centre and sales, plus a combined view. Reporting cadence proposal: weekly review in this channel, with a short written summary and any actions for the following week.

That cadence works for me. For D7, I suggest we formalise: scope is one contact centre team and one sales pod, covering top 5 contact reasons across phone, email, and chat, with a 4-week duration and a mid-point review after 2 weeks. If everyone is aligned, we can treat that as our pilot definition.
Aligned from the contact centre side. The scope and duration you summarised match what we can support operationally, and the mid-point review will help us catch any issues early.
Works for the sales pod as well. The 4-week window gives us time to adjust our approach based on the weekly KPI updates in A4.

To close D8, let us summarise the escalation criteria and SLAs: high-value leads are defined by deal size threshold, strategic accounts, urgent time-bound opportunities, or explicit customer request to speak to sales. Contact centre agents flag these in CRM using existing fields and assign them to the pilot sales pod. SLA is 2 business hours during working time, or by 10am next business day for after-hours leads. If there are no objections, we will treat this as agreed for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate learnings from pilot and confirm go-live plan for full rollout.

messages.text: Pilot completion update: the 4-week pilot with the selected sales pod and contact centre team is now complete. I have uploaded the KPI results into A4 and drafted a summary in T8, including recommendations for the unified playbook A1 and the rollout communication plan A8. Overall, conversion and data completeness improved, with a small temporary increase in handle time. In this thread, let us review the outcomes, capture key learnings for T9 and T12, and confirm whether the pilot meets the success criteria we set under D1 so we can move to full rollout.

Looking at A4, conversion from qualified lead to sale is up by 12 percent, first contact resolution improved by 8 percent, and CRM data completeness is above 95 percent for pilot teams. Average handle time increased by about 5 percent, which we expected during the transition. Quality scores based on A6 also went up. From my perspective, these results are strong enough to consider the pilot successful, but we should hear from the frontline as well.

From the contact centre team, feedback is mostly positive. Agents say A5 scripts and A2 help structure calls better, though it took a week to get comfortable. The slight increase in handle time seems to be stabilising. Transfer rate to sales went down a bit, but conversion on transferred leads went up, which suggests T10 criteria are working. I would keep the current approach and maybe add a bit more coaching on handling complex objections.

As part of the pilot sales pod, I can say the checklist in A2 and the templates in A5 made it easier to keep track of customer needs and follow-ups. At first I felt calls were a bit longer, but now they feel smoother. The only challenge I had was remembering all the escalation criteria from T10, but the decision tree in A1 helped once I got used to it.

On the sales side, opportunity qualification rate and follow-up SLA adherence both improved in A4. Reply rates on follow-up emails also ticked up. The escalation SLAs from T10 were mostly met, with a few misses in the first week that dropped after we clarified the CRM view. For T9, I suggest we capture these learnings as a short best practices section in A1 so new teams can ramp up faster.

Given the uplift in conversion, first contact resolution, and data quality, and the fact that handle time is already trending back down in week 4, I am inclined to say the pilot met the success criteria we defined under D1. The remaining gaps seem addressable through coaching and minor tweaks to A5 and A7, rather than structural changes.

I agree. The metrics in A4 are in line with or above what we targeted, and the qualitative feedback is positive. For the full rollout, I propose we keep the current scripts and checklist structure, with a few refinements based on pilot feedback, and scale the training plan A7 and communication plan A8 to all teams.

For T9, I will consolidate the final version of A1 with all approved processes, scripts, templates, and the new best practices section. I will also make sure version control and ownership are clearly documented so updates after rollout are easy to manage.

On T12, I can take the lead on refining A8 based on pilot learnings. I will highlight the key wins from A4, set expectations about the temporary handle time increase, and outline the support available during rollout. I will also tailor messages for agents, supervisors, and sales leadership.

One suggestion for the full rollout: in A7, could we add a short refresher module a few weeks after go-live. I noticed that some of the new habits only really stuck after the second or third week of the pilot.
Good idea. I will update A7 to include a follow-up refresher session for each team 3 to 4 weeks after their initial training. We can use A4 and A6 data to tailor those sessions to each team’s needs.

To explicitly address D1 for the full rollout: based on the pilot results in A4, we can say the KPIs meet or exceed the success criteria we agreed at the start. Conversion, first contact resolution, data completeness, and quality scores improved, while handle time impact is modest and trending down. I recommend we proceed with full rollout using the updated A1, A5, A7, and A8.
Aligned. From operations, I am comfortable rolling this out to all teams, as long as we keep the weekly KPI check-ins and script review sessions so we can keep improving.

Agreed. We will proceed with full rollout based on the confirmed success against D1. Next steps are to finalise A1 under T9, complete the communication plan A8 under T12, and schedule training waves per A7. I will coordinate dates with supervisors and share a rollout calendar in this channel.
